entry.title: Unexpected Credit Check Error During PGI Without an assigned Credit Segment
entry.content:
Hello Experts , 

We are experiencing an issue with the credit management setup in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud. If the Credit Segment is not maintained for the respective Sales Area, why does the system still throw a credit-related error during Post Goods Issue (PGI)?


According to the standard O2C/OTC process behavior, the absence of an assigned Credit Segment for a specific Sales Area typically indicates that credit management should not be active for that combination.

As a result, the system should not perform a credit check, and no credit-related error should occur.
However, in our current scenario, the system unexpectedly triggers a credit error during PGI, even though no Credit Segment is maintained for the Sales Area in question.

This behavior seems contrary to standard functionality, and we are trying to understand why the system enforces a credit check under these circumstances.


Is this an expected behavior under certain configurations or conditions, or could this indicate a misconfiguration? Any insights or suggestions for troubleshooting would be greatly appreciated.

entry.title: AI Search for Archived SAP KBAs: Integrating ABAP with Azure AI Search
entry.content:
Leaving SAP maintenance support does not mean losing SAP knowledge — but it does mean losing tools customers were used to.

The journey with an alternative support provider typically begins with a custom archive created from SAP software and KBA notes downloaded from the SAP Support Portal before the support contract expires. 

While this archive contains valuable corrections and documentation, access to the content becomes the customer's exclusive responsibility. Only the customer is authorized to interact with the archived material as he has the right to download and keep the copy of SAP software (according to the license terms).

For many "former" SAP support customers, this creates a long-standing challenge as such content might hardly be utilized to its full without an appropriate toolkit.

Trivial tasks like implementing a single note with prerequisites can become unexpectedly complex. In addition, most modern search engines work best with standard document formats, while a significant portion of SAP knowledge is distributed in the proprietary format zipped and packed in the .SAR file.

As a result, customers often rely on simple text extracted from .txt or .pdf files which are downloaded from the SAP Support Portal and indexed using conventional search engines.
Unfortunately, these stripped-down versions lose formatting, embedded images and other contextual information that can be crucial for determining whether a KBA is relevant and lead to solving potential SAP bug or an issue.

The result is a degraded search experience where important insights may remain hidden simply because the original structure of the document is lost.

This "workaround" has many limitations. Yet for many "former" SAP support customers it gradually becomes a new norm — learning to live with compromises.

I decided to challenge this assumption.

Instead of accepting the workaround, I set out to turn it into a proper solution and establish a new "best practice" for searching of SAP KBA in customers' archives.

The result is a solution I call SAP Archive AI Search.

1. The system leverages Microsoft Azure AI Search as the backend search engine responsible for indexing and retrieving archived content.
2. As a middleware layer I used the ABAP SDK for Azure, which I extended to support Microsoft Azure AI Search APIs.
3. Finally, a custom ABAP client provides a seamless user experience inside SAP GUI, allowing users to submit queries, navigate results, and integrate directly with other Azure services such as Blob Storage for convenient access to archived files stored in the customer’s cloud environment.

Solution is infrastructure-less, you do not need to host and run search engine on your own, distributing indexed content across the users (clients) or even use 3rd party tools to attach your cloud storage to navigate and access the content from local machines.

Only thing you need is to search for the content, read and download whatever you need straight from your SAP Gui. 

Key capabilities.

  • Unified search experience across multiple archive sources (.SAR, .TXT, .PDF)

  • United rendering using SAP GUI HTML browser controls

  • Structured index following the SAP KBA layout (Label, Symptom, Reason, Solution, etc.) allowing to address each field/section with separate set of conditions for complex query scenarios

  • Preservation of the rich formatting contained in .SAR archives including additional technical information

  • Correction instruction, enabling delta-code navigation and where-used exploration

  • Validity search, scopes your search query based on application stack of your system

  • Faceted navigation, paging, and direct reference navigation for notes present in the archive

  • Relevance scoring, including term boosting and scoring profiles dramatically improves accuracy to your search conditions

  • Full support for Azure AI Search query syntax, enabling advanced scenarios such as:

    • searching thousands of notes in a single query

    • fielded search

    • proximity, fuzzy, and regular expression queries

    • grouped queries

  • Metadata search across indexed archive attributes

Examples:

  1. Simple search retrieves all matching records per your query highlighting all found terms/tokens 

     

  2.  List overview with direct navigation to correction instruction, attachments for download and additional metadata information


  3. Use multiple conditions to search relevant notes containing DB6 in the title related to tracing using negative search list per Component field and term boosting "unix" to rank matching records containing this term on top.
  4. Search within the "delta code" of your corrections and restrict the scope per remote application stack making sure you only look for what possibly can be implemented


  5. Use expert mode to search for multiple notes in the archive and return only titles for matching records


  6. Use advance techniques like regular expression, proximity and fuzzy search whenever you need it

     



    Note: search terms in maximum proximity of two tokens apart

  7. Direct reference note navigation for the KBA articles shifts the context of your original query, however you can still navigate back using return button (vertical navigation)

    Note: Reference navigation works only for the notes which exists in your archive. 

  8. Blob search mode, allows to search and navigate based on your metadata extracted out of your blob files

 

The goal of this project was simple: restore a powerful search experience for archived SAP knowledge for customers under the 3rd party support providers.

By combining ABAP development with modern cloud search capabilities, it becomes possible to turn static SAP archives into a fully searchable knowledge system again.

I hope this approach can inspire other developers facing similar challenges which may arise along your alternative support provider.

Would like to have such solution implemented in your SAP environment?  Feel free to contact me and I will share the access to the GitHub repositories.

entry.title: Efficiency of Remote Service Connections: Redundant requests for connection details and user assignm
entry.content:
Hello,

I am looking for clarification or best practices regarding the remote connection workflow within the SAP Support Portal.

Our internal security policy dictates that remote access is restricted; we strictly open connections and assign specific users to a case only when active troubleshooting is required. Recently, we have observed a recurring pattern where, despite the connection being open and a valid user (with necessary authorizations) being assigned to the incident, SAP Support engineers repeatedly ask for connection details or confirmation of the user assignment.

This leads to unnecessary administrative overhead. We frequently find ourselves "updating" the case simply to restate that the connection is active and the user is already assigned, after which the engineer connects without further issues.

  1. Is there a known synchronization delay between the Service Marketplace/ONE Support Launchpad and the engineers' internal tools?

  2. Are there specific logs or status fields (e.g., in the SAProuter or Service Connector) we should verify to ensure the "Open" status is correctly broadcasted to SAP?

  3. Is this a procedural shift in how SAP Support handles RISE with SAP vs. On-Premise connectivity?

  4. Is this some behavior to postpone processing and get some time? Did you notice it?

Any insights on how to minimize these redundant communication loops would be appreciated.

Thank you

entry.title: AI-powered Proactive Weather Monitoring to safeguard SAP CX Utilities' Customers
entry.content:
The SAP Mission Control Center (MCC), in partnership with SAP’s Technical Support team, is launching a proactive weather-monitoring pilot program designed to protect our most critical SAP Customer Experience (CX) Utilities customers during severe weather events. Rather than waiting for tickets to surface, we proactively engage by performing advance critical health checks before a weather event makes landfall to help ensure 100% uptime for utility providers whose SAP-powered call centers are essential to emergency response operations.    

This pilot initially focuses on 5 nominated SAP Cloud for Customer (C4C) and SAP Service Cloud customers in geographically high-risk regions across North America, with the goal of providing advance warning 3-5 days before the event. 

 

The challenge: Why is severe weather critical for utilities CX?   

Utility providers are the first responders during weather-driven infrastructure failures. During a major storm event, their SAP CX platforms, particularly SAP Cloud for Customer and SAP Service Cloud, serve as the operational backbone for coordinating field crews, managing large-scale outages, and communicating with hundreds of thousands of affected customers.    

Key risk factors    

  • Sudden surges in call volume can overwhelm the call center running on SAP.    
  • Unresolved platform incidents during emergencies can directly endanger the public.
  • Traditional reactive support models may be insufficient for life-safety scenarios, underscoring the need for predictive and preventive approaches. 
  • Call center continuity is mission-critical: disruptions can impede emergency coordination.    

Our approach: proactive engagement over reactive response    

The fundamental shift in this program is a shift in posture. We move from incident-driven response   to   forecasted-risk-driven  mobilization:   proactively   identifying   threats   and deploying resources before a customer needs to raise a Priority 1 (P1) incident.    

Reactive (Old Model)

Proactive (Our Approach)

Wait for the customer to raise a P1

Monitor weather threats 3–5 days in advance

 

Mobilize SAP MCC resources after the event

Activate Critical Period Coverage (CPC) proactively prior to landfall

How it works: monitor, assess, and activate our Critical Period Coverage portfolio offering  

The program follows a 3-phase period coverage activation.   

Step 1: Monitor

AI tools continuously scan authoritative weather data feeds for the geographic regions associated with each pilot customer. Monitoring runs daily and continuously throughout the pilot period.

Step 2: Assess

When a potential threat is identified, the system determines the  geographic impact area, event duration, severity, and proximity to each customer’s service territory. This produces a per-customer risk score.   

Step 3: Activate the SAP MCC Critical Period Coverage offering

If the risk score exceeds the activation threshold, the critical period coverage is triggered. The SAP MCC assigns a Critical Customer Manager to the account who acts as the single point of contact, notifies the account team and, if necessary, the customer, and begins active monitoring of system utilization and incident queues for the duration of the event.

 Collaboration across LoBs

The SAP MCC aligns with experts from the SAP Technical Support organization and the CX Operations teams to determine whether the system is adequately sized and whether scale-up or sizing changes are required.  In addition, the SAP MCC will collaborate with Technical Support to review the customer’s configuration and run proactive health checks in advance of the event to proactively mitigate risk and help maintain 100% uptime during the storm.   

Post-event, the SAP MCC will document the engagement, capture lessons learned, and channel findings back into the program to improve risk scoring and response thresholds.    

AI-powered weather intelligence - Powered by AI / Joule

The   3-to-5-day   warning   window   is   made   possible   by   an   AI-assisted monitoring layer that continuously ingests real-time and forecast weather data and correlates it with the precise geographic footprint of each pilot customer’s service territory.

How the AI layer works:   
Continuous Weather Monitoring

  • AI tools (powered by Claude/Joule Studio) continuously ingest real-time and forecast weather data feeds from authoritative sources, with algorithms that identify events matching defined severity and geographic thresholds.
  • Daily  alerts  are  automatically  issued  to  prevent  missed  events,  while
    notifications are triggered 3-5 days before landfall and delivered directly via email and mobile.   

Customer Risk Assessment & Scoring   

  • Customer service regions are mapped to storm tracks to determine the likelihood of impact.    
  • Duration, intensity, and affected population density are factored into a composite risk model. Joule evaluates and provides a risk percentage for threats to critical infrastructure based on the weather event/region and produces a ranked per- customer risk score that defines the critical period coverage activation level. 

Communications Generation   

  • Internal and external communications are automatically generated based on the ongoing weather event and reported customer issues, ensuring timely and consistent messaging throughout the event lifecycle.

Customer Incident Dashboard   

  • A real-time customer incident dashboard is created and actively monitored throughout the duration of the critical period coverage.   
  • This is powered by SAP Joule providing a centralized view of customer impact, open incidents, and status tracking.   

Pilot scope: 5 focus CX utilities customers    

The initial pilot focuses on 5 SAP Customer Experience customers across Florida, California, Arkansas, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Texas and Virginia.

These customers were nominated based on weather exposure, geographic risk profile and business criticality. The primary focus is on call center deployments which is directly linked to emergency response capability.

What to expect

When the SAP MCC identifies a threat   

  • SAP MCC will proactively reach out to the SAP Customer Success Manager 3–5 days before a forecast event. 
  • The front office teams will receive event details: affected region, severity, expected duration, and the customer risk score. 
  • A named SAP MCC resource will be introduced as the dedicated contact for the critical period coverage (customer-facing if appropriate). 

During the event   

  • The SAP MCC will communicate directly with the customer contact to streamline the response. 
  • SAP Technical Support will run health checks to help ensure 100% system uptime during the event. 

The account team will be copied on all critical communications and escalation notifications.   

After the event   

  • The SAP Mission Control Center will debrief with the front office team and document the engagement. Feedback is used to improve the risk scoring model for future events.    

A special thanks to Daniel Gerdes - SVP and Head of the SAP Mission Control Center, Hari Doraisamy - Head of the SAP Mission Control Center North America,  Srivatsa V - Head of Support, Sales & Service Cloud, Usha Krishnakumar - Solution area lead SAP Mission Control Center, Joe Gamble - Solution area lead SAP Mission Control Center for their contributions to this article.
